reviews.text: Tl;dr 8.5/10 so far Imagine if you took Risk of Rain, Vampire Survivors, and Crab Champions, and combined them into one. That is essentially Atomic Picnic in a nutshell. The game takes the third-person shooter aspect of RoR, combines it with the upgrade system of VS, and layers on top of it the momentum and speed of character movement in CC. The result is pretty awesome. You can play this game co-op or solo. The game has a roguelite meta progression in the form of "Mementos", which are your typical meta upgrades like +damage, movement speed, etc. The boss fights in this game are pretty good and can be quite challenging without any mementos. I recommend you pick up all of the side objective rewards and collect pebbles as they appear to build up your character asap, especially early on when you don't have mementos. This game is launching in early access right now. In the future, I would like to see more characters, guns, devices, upgrades, bosses, etc. Just more! The foundation is super solid, movement feels slick and responsive, and the gunplay is great for this type of game. GIVE US MORE BITCAKE! WE LOVE IT! Disclosure - I assisted in publishing this game and have been giving feedback on it for a while

I've been playing since the early playtests and you can tell the amount of work they've been doing since then. The movement is a huge highlight for me, even compared to games like Risk of Rain 2 I feel like I just have more control over dodging and running around when it gets hectic. They've also done a good job improving the visual clarity of incoming damage. A big issue early on for me was not knowing if I was standing in an enemy's attack, especially when aiming up, but they've tweaked the indicators and camera to where it's no longer a problem. I'd highly suggest giving Atomic Picnic a try if you enjoy the genre. There's a lot to like here for an Early Access game.

[quote] Please consider following my [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/41005226/]Curation page[/url]. I cover a wide range of genres both paid and unpaid, providing unbiased opinions as well as regular giveaway events. [/quote] [b]Video Review[/b] https://youtu.be/6-Iy9A0lxgE [H2]Could be better[/h2] The gameplay is a little shaky at times, and the longer you progress through the events (there is no timer), the lower the frame rate becomes for some enemies, such as snakes or snacks, due to a wrong translation of the name. Every tree has a safe zone and if you stand on the ledge of any terrain it's the same thing, therefore stepping on one makes you invulnerable; creatures will spawn just on top of you, unable to target you. So this makes the gameplay exploitable, buggy, unpolished and unfinished. It does not appear to be very rewarding in its current state, as you can play for 30-40 minutes and not succeed because it is the type of game that requires 5 - 6 hours of farming to acquire the materials needed for increased damage, items, unlock classes, and so on. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] It plays great similarly to how Risk of Rain 2 does especially with the flow of movement and dashes, but it doesn't function very well due to the bugs and balancing concerns due to mob density later on throughout the stage. I don't think a game like this is worth the price currently; lower the price in half or wait til they fix the games issues first, and then you'd have a highly engaging and exciting swarm like game with great Roguelike elements. There doesn't seem to be an online mode currently, unless that's also hidden behind unlocks I am unaware of. You can take this review as more of a informational one, actually think this game has a lot going for it, it's just not where it needs to be as of right now. Hopefully the developers take feedback and polish it out some more for a later date.

[h1]NOTE ABOUT OTHER REVIEWS:[/h1] There are a bunch of reviews that complain that the game is broken because it doesn't have a reload button... This is VERY CLEARLY intentional since there are very powerful items that work on reloads. This means that you can build your way to having a small magazine size or high fire rate to activate on reload effects more frequently. The people who complain about that either didn't really play the game or are not much smarter than a chipmunk. Really neat action Roguelike game. Plays mostly like Risk of Rain 2 with smoother controls and better movement Loot economy and progression is mostly like Vampire Survivors You can choose different characters with upgradeable skills, weapons and gadgets as your loadout which can vary your runs a bit. During your run there will be different objectives you need to complete to win and a bunch of helpful events for loot or health etc. which makes it a little bit more varied than the other 2 games I mentioned. I have encountered exactly 1 bug in over 5 hours of playtime which is more than fine with me for a early access title. Now to some negatives: The balance of items, weapons and gadgets is way off. There is a clearly best option for every category that just overshadows the rest. This can easily be fixed with some number changes in the future though. The enemies can be a tad annoying. There is an enemy time that will just teleport behind you all the time no matter how far away you try to escape. There are flying enemies that shoot very frequently and drop bombs on you that spawn in truly ridiculous amounts and are just a little bit too tanky. Take this with a grain of salt since it's pretty subjective. When you zoom in with the sniper your scope will be way off the 3rd person crosshair, which drives me crazy. All in all: Could be my new favorite action roguelike in the future. The content that's here is great just a little sparse. It's more than worth the 20€ that it costs right now though. I'm looking forward for new weapons, gadgets and items.

The core gameplay is fun. But right now, I can't recommend this game to any audience other than hardcore single players or groups that play together. As an average single player, I'm up for a grind (playing Witchfire, DRGS with at least medium success) - but right here, I'm hitting a wall just with the second tutorial mission, "get to lvl 10". Whatever skills I use, it doesn't make any difference, I get killed at enemy level 8 or 9. I've unlocked a couple of meta upgrades, they don't offer sense of progression. The developers claim, the game is intentionally "very hard", but this is not "very hard", this is just bad design. Give me smaller and meaningful steps of improvements and I will accept "very hard". Game also feels very beta-ish and and has A LOT of rough edges. For now, I'm handing in a refund, because it makes no sense for me playing the game. Might come back some time in the future.

I don't even know where to begin..... Friend of mine and I play a lot of rogelike games and they recommended we try this one today, it looked promising at first but the experience has been....mixed at best so far. Let's start with the positives: 1. The art and sound design are great, everything looks good and the BGM/SFX really do make things engaging as the chaos ensues around you. It's fun seeing the results of your build go wild on your screen and decimate groups of enemies, one of the main things I look forward to in a roguelike game. 2. Each weapon feels very unique and different which is something I do appreciate in games like this as you usually end up with a bunch of barely different gameplay experiences between weapon archetypes, that is thankfully not the case here....I'm a fan of how the shotgun and AR play in particular. 3. It is easy to get overpowered quickly if you know what to pick, cursed curious in particular allow to you forgo one stat in favor of min/maxing another to an absurd degree and getting some very interesting results. And now for the (unfortunately) long and crippling list of negatives.... 1. This game's difficulty is imbalanced....like to a hairbrained degree, especially early on. Everything feels insanely tanky before level 10 and when you reach that point you're either on your way to becoming a force of nature or about to die horribly to the four enemies that spawn for your first hurdle. I'd like to say this remedies itself as things go on but unless you get a bunch of healing curious (of which there is exactly one reliable option) you're just not able to keep up with the damage going out and forced to pass revives back and forth between you and your partner...and that's IF you have a partner. From what I can tell there doesn't seem to be any difference in enemy density if you're solo or co-op so the solo experience is....abysmal to say the least. Is it impossible? No....but it's close, as things stand if something doesn't change there may as well not be a solo experience at all because you're teetering on the brink of death constantly in this game. Like not even Risk of Rain on monsoon makes me feel this fragile and that's just insane to me.... 2. Curios seem tailor made for the AR and only the AR, every other weapon (with the exception of maybe the pistol) just flat doesn't get enough out of them to perform as the game goes on. The minigun one in particular is just useless unless you're using the AR which is disheartening because it's quite fun on that gun. This needs to change...quickly, guns need to have some dedicated curios that only spawn for them and enhance what they're good at because as it stands you just aren't going to cut it with a weapon based build on any other weapon. 3. The unlock conditions for other characters are absurd......or at least the two I've discovered. Taking 12k damage will eventually happen passively but at four hours I have barely over 3k, and the other I've discovered? 80 last second dodges through an attack...of which I had four before I started actively trying to get them done. Got that number to 10 in my next run before dying horribly since it's just not realistic to dodge like that with the amount of insanity going on. I don't know if it's random based on what type of attack I'm dodging or they're expecting Fromsoft game last second precision for this one but as it stands there's no way I'm going to get this done without actively sitting in front of fliers and dodging those little orbs for hours before I eventually die of boredom (or a stray enemy charging at me out of nowhere). These types of achievements usually get you cosmetics or other prestige awards...not other playable characters. If they expect me to play just one for 20-40 hours before I eventually meet one of these arbitrary requirements they're out of their mind... And the last (and worst) glaring issue.... 4. Bugs and performance issues....tons of them. The game runs butter smooth at max settings early on, even when I was sending out a constant stream of homing/exploding/ricochet rounds from my AR and watching swathes of enemies die horribly things didn't seem to slow down one bit....then we got to the boss. Immediately the sound cut out and our characters became invisible (as well as the boss but.....it's a chameleon so that may have been intended). Models were flickering in and out for a few minutes before my friend was booted and I abruptly got stuck in some terrain and died....they didn't get to keep any of the currency we got that run, and this wasn't even the only time this happened. Next run? The moment the boss spawns I happen to be jumping next to a tree and my character just lands next to it and becomes frozen in place...unable to act or move. I eventually die and am subsequently revived by my partner only to still be unable to move before a game mechanic that kills you if you're not close enough to the boss kills us both and ends the run there. ...and the next? I made a grenade build...which was honestly pretty fun for a while but the moment I got my cooldown reduction low enough to get a one second CD on them all the sound cuts out and performance instantly throttles into the ground, freezing up before booting my friend again and crashing. There were just as many particles on screen (if not fewer) as when I was using my AR bullet hell build from before. And this just continues...each time we made it to the Chameleon boss the game just loses its mind and sound/visuals take a nosedive in quality for both of us (if they work at all)....eventually the both of us just got fed up and quit, unable to justify banging our heads against every other issue this has in hopes we'd eventually get a clean shot to bring it down. It's really disheartening because I do think this game has potential to be fun, the audio and visuals are still great and what does work works very well...but there's just too much working against it as is to justify playing any more right now. This needs a very thorough patch and soon....buy at your own risk.

I love roguelike games. With experience of games like : Risk of Rain, Gunfire Reborn, Immortal Redneck, Roboquest, Returnal and many other with rogue-like/lite elements i have a few words to share about current state of Atomic Picnic Keep in mind that game is in Early Access, have constant patches and very dedicated Devs What i like about Atomic Picnic : - Simple but nice looking graphics - Responsive movement - Character and map design - Game Setting - Multiplayer - Communication between player base and Developers What i dont like about the game at current state : - Lack of content Curios / maps / enemies / end-game / challange / game mods / bosses - Upgrade system There is no real need to use it, game dont have content that challange you or requires some grind before you can complete it. - Balance Once you found about curio combination, you can alsmost afk through the game and succesfully complete every run. Upgrades , weapon, character choice doesnt matter. - Achievments and conditions to unlock weapons/characters 4 hours - this much time it took me to complete all present maps in the game, 6 more hours i have grinded last map to gather some resources. How many characters i have unlocked you ask me ? None. I still have only first character that you start game with and dont need anything else to complete the game. Conditions to unlock characters is overtuned, they require too much time and effort to complete, which is totaly unnecessary. Requirements are just boring : Take 12000 damage, dodge direct attack 80 times, etc... I know you may unlock character eventually but i have tried specifically work towards progression for character i like and only got half way though after 10 hours. - Performance issues My PC specs are high end ( 7800x3d + 7900xtx ) On 2K resolution with high graphic settings i have around 90 fps with frame drops on game progression. Once you get some specific curio combination, reduce cooldowns or increase aoe, you are no longer playing smooth game. - Objectives Stay in 3 circles for fixed amount of time dodging air barrage and repeat it twice in order to complete a map. This is just player time wasting. Also it is hard to visually locate exact place where you need to be once event on map is present What can help in the current game state ? I hope in the near future we will have end game features which will help to retain player base, such as custom difficulty. Give me more % of exp and currency in exchange of higher monster density, more monster health / damage / projectiles / aoe / defence and so on. This will drasticaly improve experience of players and will make upgrades viable. There is no difference between 1'st and 4'th maps. The only difference in time of the day. You can just remove 4'th map, change concept of the Night in maps to special difficulty mode and call it something like : Middnight Picnic ( hard verison of map ). Maps will look more dark with stronger enemies and harder challanges. This will add additional layer of content to the game. Today 14.11.2024, few days after my initial review developers made other characters more accessible. Its still takes more time than i would prefer to unlock them, but its way better than was before - kudos for listening to the comunity! ✓ Add more information / explanations to specific stats and how they affect gameplay, before players unlock them in the shop with representative mementos As for now : Every Picnic is the same I will continue to keep my eye on the game development with a hope that my review will change in near future. I want this project to succeed and will continue supporting developers. Whoever you are, thank you for reading my review and remember, its always better to try the game yourself.

[h1]We would like to thank the developers for providing us a copy of this game for reviewing purposes[/h1] I am going to start off by saying that this review is going to hurt me while writing this, as I do think there is a great game here. However, in its current state, I can’t recommend [b]Atomic Picnic[/b], and this is coming from someone who has played a lot of shooters in their time. When I received a free copy for review of this game, I was hyped, the game looked fantastic and fun to play but a bunch of problems held it back from me enjoying it. [h1]Pros and Cons[/h1] [b]Pros[/b] [list] [*]Gameplay is fun [*]The visuals are nice to look at [/list] [b]Cons[/b] [list] [*]The game’s balance is a mess, enemies will kill you in two or three hits sometimes [*]There are too many projectiles for you to dodge sometimes [*]Upgrades are very lackluster to use [*]Enemies will spawn right next to you [*]The game will not explain certain things and give little info [/list] [h1]Gameplay[/h1] The one thing I will say that is good about [b]Atomic Picnic's[/b] gameplay is that it’s good, the shooting is fluid, and your character moves very well. There are multiple characters for you to play as but I have been only able to play as one and I’ll explain why in a bit. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3384053794 All the characters have abilities that they can utilize in combat, you have a dash that you can use to get the move on enemies. When an enemy dies, they will drop experience points, which you can use to level up, from there, you can select from three different upgrades. These help you out in combat, slightly, while useful, a large majority of them are underwhelming and certain upgrades are just straight-up better or are required to even get decently far in the level you are in. I’ll get back to this sort of thing later on in the review. The balancing in this game is terrible, enemies can pretty much kill you in a few hits and you don’t do enough damage to help take out the tanky ones. The enemies have attacks that can kill you in two or three hits if you are not careful. There are also way too many projectiles for you to avoid sometimes or too many enemies for you to really deal with at a time, due to you only having a single-shot weapon. You don’t have access to a secondary at all and are only left with one gun, grenades, and a special attack. The other characters may have something different to them but I haven’t had the chance to play them yet. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3384047818 Also, in case anyone wants to say to me that this is a skill issue, I just want to point out that shooters are one of the main genres of games that I play. I have played [b]Team Fortress 2[/b] for at least 13 years, played [b]Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands[/b] on hard mode, and completed [b]Warhammer Space Marine[/b] (the first game) on hard mode. [b]Warhammer Space Marine[/b] is a much more punishing game than this one too. So in case anyone wants to question my legitimacy on this, I have the proof right here and I can show off more examples if necessary. [b]Atomic Picnic[/b] advertises itself as a casual shooter, not a hardcore one. Now I can talk about the upgrades, they are very lackluster, and the good ones, don’t do enough to help you. Some of them are just mandatory for you to get anywhere in this game. You can level up the upgrades to offer more utility, but the problem is that, even then, they don’t do enough to help you. Some of them are also not very interesting or not worthwhile to use either. There isn’t an effective way to heal yourself, there are these [b]green crystals[/b] that can heal you and an upgrade that gives you a small chance to heal yourself when taking out an enemy, although it only heals one HP. There are a select few upgrades that are cused, that offer an extra benefit but at the cost of reducing the stats on your character. The issue with this is that it’s not worth it, if your stats get lowered like damage, you are just shooting yourself in the foot because enemies are pretty tanky. Sometimes enemies will spawn right next to you, the devs did state that they fixed this issue but sometimes I do get some enemies that will still do it. There is also no indicator of where you are taking damage or when enemies are around you. Enemies are so tanky that some require an entire magazine to take out. There are also zones you can go to but the game won’t explain what to do in them, this game has a bunch of stuff that they don’t explain. There seems to be a lot to this game, but the lack of explanation makes this entire game hard to play. There is one thing that can make this game easier to play and that is having some friends to play with, although I have none that play this game, so I am out of luck. [h1]Graphics and Performance[/h1] [b]Atomic Picnic[/b] does have some very nice visuals, the colors are very pretty and look good. I tested the game on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, and 16 GB of RAM, I had no issues while I was playing. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3384048051 [h1]Final Verdict[/h1] [b]Atomic Picnic[/b] is a fun game, but it’s held back by a bunch of design problems that are preventing me from enjoying it. I do think this game has some clever ideas, but it needs more time in the oven. If you want a game that makes you fight a bunch of enemies with worthwhile upgrades, then [b]Vampire Survivors[/b] is the game for you, and it’s priced at 5.99 CDN. However, I do think this game can be worth it when more updates come out, the devs do seem passionate about it and are still updating it. While I don’t recommend [b]Atomic Picnic[/b] now, I do think the game will be much better when it’s worked on more. [quote]Looking for more reviews like this one? Then follow [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/5297658/]Life Needs a Little Sin [/url][/quote]

With a first major update none of the core issues have been fixed. Solo is still borderline unplayable, most of the powerups you get either do nothing meaningful or not enough. You can only progress game with extremely specific build of best powerups, there is no room for improvisation, trying something new or just getting unlucky choices. Fun concept, terrible roguelike part implemention. As of April 8th: the game still runs like absolute crap - you may have 100fps, but it doesn't matter because game just keeps skipping frames making it feel like you have 10 when there is like 10+ monsters on screen. Meta unlocks range from unimpactful to straight up barely playable - imagine having low fire rate, slow moving projectiles affected by gravity against endless swarms of air units. and best part, you randomly lose half of the stuff you unlocked before between patches that haven't even made changes to unlocks you had. As for roguelike in match powerups - its pretty much you either get all on hit effects with your rerols or you can restart, since most of them does barely anything in terms of actually killing anything. [後半に日本語レビューあり] [h1]A 3D Co-op Survivors-like Roguelite TPS[/h1] Set in a post-apocalyptic wasteland devastated by the "Harvest Festival" explosion, this is a third-person cooperative roguelite shooter. Supporting up to four players in online co-op, each run — called a "Picnic" — has players mowing down monster hordes while building out their loadouts. The standout feature is how the game translates wave-survival gameplay into a fully 3D space. The "Impulse Gear" system — swinging, dashing, and double-jumping — mitigates the flat monotony that traditional Survivors-like games tend to suffer from. Raining fire from high ground, dodging off cliffs, and launching from ramps all feel great, giving the verticality of each arena real purpose (personally, I also felt echoes of Risk of Rain 2's vertical tension). At the heart of buildcrafting lies the "Curio" system. Players equip up to eight passive abilities gained on level-up during a run, and maxing specific Curio combinations can trigger powerful "Evolutions." "Cursed Curios" add a gambling element with random positive and negative stat modifiers, and the experimentation across runs gives each Picnic a distinct identity. The colorful anime-styled visuals are appealing, though some Early Access roughness remains. Level-up rewards can feel incremental — small percentage boosts that don't always deliver that satisfying power spike. The development team's community-driven approach through Discord is notable, with consistent major updates including full balance overhauls being delivered regularly. For players seeking the thrill of Survivors-like gameplay with 3D verticality and cooperative fun, this is arguably an Early Access title worth watching as it continues to evolve. ATOMIC PICNIC INTRO Atomic Picnic is a third-person bullet heaven that mixes fast-paced combat with explosive co-op action. You’re swinging, dashing, and blasting through waves of enemies while stacking upgrades and building some pretty ridiculous combinations. At least… that’s how the game describes itself. So today, we’re going to take a closer look at Atomic Picnic and see if it’s actually fun — or if it just sounds good on paper. Before we get into it, I do want to mention that this game was gifted to me by the publisher, Mad Mushroom. That said, this isn’t a sponsored review, and there were no requirements on what I could or couldn’t say and no requirement to even play or make this review — so everything here is my honest opinion as always. Also this game is in early access so i will try to re review the game upon launch GAMEPLAY Atomic Picnic is a roguelite, survivors-like game where you choose from multiple characters, each with their own look and unique ultimate ability. There’s also a variety of weapons to pick from — assault rifles, snipers, shotguns, grenade launchers, pistols, bows — and you can mix any character with any weapon, which opens up a lot of different playstyles. Each character can be upgraded over time to become stronger, but instead of having a full skill tree, the game uses a more straightforward upgrade path that just improves their overall power. Weapons can also be customized with attachments, which add different effects and change how they behave during a run. You also have grenades one thats regular, one thats fire or ice As for unlocking everything, most characters and weapons are tied to challenges. A lot of these will be completed naturally just by playing, while others require a bit more effort and intention to unlock. There are also “mementos,” which are essentially special upgrades you can find during a run. Once you’ve unlocked them, you can upgrade them using what the game calls pebbles — or at least I think that’s what they’re called. It kind of looks like gold, so… gold pebbles, I guess. Upgrading them increases the buffs they give, making them more effective in future runs. There’s also a discovery page where you can see everything you’ve unlocked, along with what you’re still missing. If you hover over items that are close to being unlocked, the game tells you exactly what you need to do. But if it’s something you’re not even close to unlocking yet, it just shows this unreadable, almost alien-looking text instead. As for the actual gameplay loop — it’s pretty straightforward. You pick a map (starting with one and unlocking more as you progress), choose your character, weapon, and grenade, and then jump into a run. From there, each map follows a similar structure. You fight enemies to level up, then complete a set of main objectives: escorting the rover, planting bombs to destroy a pillar, fighting a zone guardian, and finally taking on the map boss through a portal. Although on the first map, there doesn’t seem to be a proper boss — just the guardian. As you level up during a run, you pick upgrades just like in other survivors-like games, and that essentially forms the core gameplay loop. The bosses are pretty cool, and each one has its own unique fight. That said, they do feel a bit easy once you learn their mechanics. My favorite so far is the bird boss, Oswald — mainly because the fight feels the most unique, and it was actually the most challenging out of all of them. The game also has a fast reload mechanic. When you run out of ammo, a quick-time event appears that lets you reload faster if you hit it correctly. You also don't need to reload until you actually completely run out of ammo as your ammo will regenerate if you don't shoot. At first, I thought this was kind of pointless… but it actually grew on me. Especially because there are upgrades that trigger effects when you fast reload. And once you unlock the upgrade that makes fast reloading automatic, those effects become even more powerful, which is a nice touch. As for the upgrades overall, they’re decent — but I do feel like there’s a lack of variety. Some of them are pretty cool. For example, instead of a typical slow effect you’d see in most games like this, this one spawns a snowman that slows enemies down. So while the ideas aren’t completely new, the game does put its own spin on them. That said, there just aren’t enough options right now, and it makes build variety feel a bit limited. The game also has “cursed” upgrades, which I actually like. They come with both upsides and downsides, so it feels like you’re shaping a more specific build by sacrificing certain stats for others. But some of these don’t feel fully thought out — either they don’t really have a meaningful downside, or they don’t feel like much of an upgrade at all. And in some cases, the descriptions aren’t very clear about what they are actually doing. Unfortunately this game does not have a endless mode or atleast if it does i never found it which means each run last about 15 or so mins and it would just be way nicer in my opinion to have an option for endless mode that gets harder and harder as time goes by GRAPHICS The graphics are very stylistic, leaning into more of an anime aesthetic. If you like that style, you’ll probably enjoy how the game looks — and if you don’t, then it likely won’t do much for you. Personally, I do like the overall art style. OUTRO So overall, the gameplay is fun. The movement feels good, the guns feel good, and the progression is solid. But it does feel like it’s lacking variety — especially when it comes to upgrades. The game also has co-op, which, like most games, naturally makes the experience more fun. There are a few minor bugs and glitches. I haven’t personally run into many, but some players have reported issues like the game’s sound cutting out, which can be pretty annoying. There are also no achievements in the game at the moment, although I’d expect those to be added in the future. I also want to talk about the price — it currently sits at $20, and honestly, I think that’s a bit too much right now. The game is fun, but I don’t think there’s quite enough content to justify that price at the moment, especially since it’s expected to increase at full release which means the game will be $25 to $30 at launch. That puts it in a slightly awkward spot, because it’s competing with games like Risk of Rain 2, Roboquest, Gunfire Reborn, and others — games that are in that price point, but offer significantly more content and replayability in my opinion. So at the end of the day, the game is fun and has a lot of potential… but the pricing doesn’t quite match what’s currently on offer but it fun.
